title: Probing Synthetic Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon States Through Critical Current in Full-Shell Nanowire Josephson Junctions
authors: Carlos Payá, Ángel Ibabe, Mario Gómez, Thomas Kanne, Jesper Nygård, Ramón Aguado, Pablo San-Jose, Eduardo J. H. Lee, Elsa Prada
abstract: Full-shell hybrid nanowires consisting of a semiconductor core fully enveloped by a superconducting shell have emerged as a platform to study Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) analogs. These subgap states can be considered a synthetic version of CdGM states in Abrikosov vortices. Unlike conventional CdGM states, these analogs exhibit a level spacing comparable to the superconducting gap, making them readily observable via tunneling spectroscopy techniques. The spectral density of CdGM analogs follows a characteristic skewed pattern as a function of applied axial magnetic field, an effect that is superimposed on the Little-Parks oscillations of the shell's gap induced by fluxoid quantization. Here, we provide experimental evidence for CdGM analogs through a distinctive skewness fingerprint in the critical current and zero-bias resistance of overdamped Josephson junctions based on full-shell nanowires.
summary: The authors investigate synthetic Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states in full-shell nanowire Josephson junctions. By measuring the critical current ($I_c$) under an applied magnetic field, they observe a distinct skewness pattern. This signature is theoretically linked to CdGM analogs within the semiconductor core, providing strong evidence for their existence and utility as a diagnostic tool for superconducting physics.
main_problem: The study aims to experimentally probe synthetic Caroli-de Gennes-Matricon (CdGM) states within full-shell nanowire Josephson junctions.
main_result: The characteristic skewness observed in the critical current ($I_c$) and zero-bias resistance ratio ($R_0/R_N$) is attributed to these CdGM analogs residing in the semiconductor core, superimposed on Little-Parks oscillations from the superconducting shell.
method: The research combines transport measurements (measuring $dI/dV$ vs. $B$ and $I$) with microscopic theoretical modeling using Keldysh Green's functions formalism.
model_or_system: The physical system is a full-shell hybrid nanowire Josephson junction ($	ext{SC}/	ext{SM}$ core). The model uses a tight-binding Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian to calculate observables like the Local Density of States (LDOS) and critical current.
key_observables: Critical current ($I_c$) skewness, zero-bias resistance ratio ($R_0/R_N$), Little-Parks oscillations in $dI/dV$, and superconducting gap modulation.
important_parameters: Axial magnetic field ($B$), superconducting gap ($\Delta$), flux quantum ($\Phi_0$), and the level spacing of CdGM analogs relative to $\Delta$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the observed skewness is dominated by the finite population of CdGM analogs crossing zero energy, rather than just shell gap collapse.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $dI/dV$ vs. $B$ showing Little-Parks lobes and current skewness; other figures compare theoretical predictions for $I_c$ skewness against experimental data derived from the $R_0/R_N$ ratio.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the physical platform (full-shell nanowires) and the phenomenon of CdGM analogs. It presents measurements showing characteristic current modulation and asymmetry, which are then theoretically modeled using Green's functions to confirm that the skewness fingerprint uniquely identifies the presence of these subgap states.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental realization and diagnostic tool (the $I_c$ skewness) for studying exotic superconducting phenomena like CdGM states, which are highly relevant in mesoscopic superconductivity and topological materials research.
